The trial court found the chicken litter clause was unconscionable,

summary judgment, and entered judgment in favor of Buyers on Stoll's

ANALYSIS 
Stoll argues the trial court erred in finding the chicken litter clause 
was unconscionable as a matter oflaw, "by considering the fairness of the 
contract," and by considering "anything other than fraud, duress, undue 
influence, mistake, or illegality of the contract." He claims the trial court 
should have recognized "the validity of the contract at issue" and granted 
him judgment as a matter of law.
